title: Invariant expansion coefficients from a twisted tensor comparison
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings and $\sigma,\tau:A\to B$ unital ring homomorphisms. Let $D=B\otimes_{\sigma,A,\tau}B$, using $\sigma$ on the first factor and $\tau$ on the second [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with its tensor-product ring structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Put $p_0(b)=b\otimes1$, $p_1(b)=1\otimes b$. Suppose a ring homomorphism $\Delta:B\to D$ satisfies $\Delta\sigma=p_1\sigma$ and $\Delta\tau=p_0\tau$. Let $r\geq1$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in A$. Assume $(\tau(x_j))_{j=1}^r$ is an $A$-basis of $B$ through $\sigma$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], meaning every $b\in B$ has a unique expansion $b=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$ with $a_j\in A$. Then $(p_0(\tau(x_j)))_{j=1}^r$ is a $B$-basis of $D$ through $p_1$. Moreover, for every $a\in A$, the unique coefficients $a_j$ in $\tau(a)=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$ satisfy $\sigma(a_j)=\tau(a_j)$ for every $j$.

source.place: Tag 03C8 (groupoids-lemma-basis), second diagram, left vertical isomorphism and coefficientwise equalizer comparison; old proof steps 3-4.

proof.text: Give the first copy of $B$ its $A$-module structure through $\sigma$ and the second its $A$-algebra structure through $\tau$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] to the assumed basis $e_j=\tau(x_j)$ of the first copy. Its right-tensor form says that $(e_j\otimes1)_j=(p_0(\tau(x_j)))_j$ is a basis of $D$ over the second copy of $B$, whose scalar action is multiplication through $p_1$. This proves the first conclusion; write this basis as $(E_j)_j.

source.place: Tag 03C8 (groupoids-lemma-basis), second commutative diagram: left vertical basis isomorphism and coefficientwise comparison.

proof.text: For a fixed $a\in A$, write its assumed unique expansion $\tau(a)=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$. The tensor balancing relation gives $p_0(\sigma(u))=\sigma(u)\otimes1=1\otimes\tau(u)=p_1(\tau(u))$ for every $u\in A$. The ring structure makes $p_0,p_1$ ring maps. Apply $\Delta$ to the expansion and use the two assumed identities to obtain $p_0(\tau(a))=\sum_jp_1(\sigma(a_j))E_j$. Apply $p_0$ to the same expansion and use the balancing identity to obtain $p_0(\tau(a))=\sum_jp_1(\tau(a_j))E_j$. Both are expansions over the second copy of $B$ in exactly the same basis.

source.place: Tag 03C8 (groupoids-lemma-basis), second commutative diagram: left vertical basis isomorphism and coefficientwise comparison.

proof.text: By the uniqueness clause in the definition of a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], the two coefficient vectors in step 2 are equal as vectors with entries in $B$: their $j$th entries are $\sigma(a_j)$ and $\tau(a_j)$. Hence $\sigma(a_j)=\tau(a_j)$ for every $j$. The argument applies to each $a\in A$ and proves the second conclusion.
